correctness.rationale: Here N=g−I has N³=0 and its square has only block XY. Conjugation moves only Z, by the image of the map (X′,Y′) ↦ XY′−X′Y up to an immaterial sign. The two summand images have dimensions cr and as and intersect in the rs-dimensional maps from the c-space modulo ker Y into im X. Thus t=cr+as−rs. To count a rank-s image U of Y for fixed X, choose U∩ker X of dimension s−k and its k-dimensional projection modulo ker X; after choosing a splitting the possible lifts are the graphs into ker X/(U∩ker X). This gives exactly the stated Gaussian factors, bounds and power of q. Each image has S_q(c,s) surjective lifts, and Z is free. Both invariants are conjugacy invariant, validating division by q^t. In the limit t≤ac since ac−t=(a−r)(c−s), and conditional on full row rank of X, t=ac and XY is exactly uniform. The complement's probability bounds total variation. In characteristic two the square determines whether the order is four because N³=0. Independent enumeration of actual distinct conjugation displacements, not ranks of commutator matrices, agreed with every joint cell in three small prime-field cases; in the stated q=2 example the t=4 cells were 192, 1728 and 576.
residual_risks: The independent small census is over prime fields only. The proof uses finite-field vector spaces and has no prime-field restriction.

originality.rationale: Credit the positive-square-rank refinement of the one-element class-size census for general blocks and the corresponding fixed-end joint law, not the already covered even-characteristic zero-square slice, the class exponent on that slice, or total class counts. The closest prior zero-product incidence imposes containment in the kernel and hence does not account for noncontained images, which are needed in each positive-k bin. The bounded primary-source comparison did not establish an exact dominating all-rank joint census.
residual_risks: The literature on exact ranks of products of independent rectangular finite-field matrices may contain further equivalent conditional incidence formulas. The comparison does not certify exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: The class size controls orbit counting, and the square rank is a natural nilpotent invariant that distinguishes order at most two from order four in even characteristic. The exact refinement for arbitrary block sizes captures new positive-rank information within a single class-size stratum, rather than merely reprinting a total or the known zero-square slice. It gives both element and class counts for these invariants and quantifies the persistence of distinct square ranks as the class size concentrates.
residual_risks: This is not a classification of individual classes or an assertion about parabolic conjugacy or longer flags.
